races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: Dominant front-runner with four wins from her last five starts over 10f, all on good ground; the soft is a mild query on breeding but her class and Tim Easterby's red-hot 14-day record (6/79) compensate, and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim keeps weight manageable at 140lbs.|
runners_data.comment: Poet's Dawn arrives on the back of three wins in his last six starts, including back-to-back victories three and four starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the risk is that his last two runs have yielded a seventh and a ninth, raising questions about current form.

runners_data.name: Triple Force
runners_data.note: Returning after 66 days off, which is a genuine fitness concern, though Craig Lidster has placed him over 10-12f on good ground repeatedly; needs to prove he is fully wound up before this can be taken seriously as a front-running threat.|

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with five places from his last six runs including two seconds over similar trips; soft-going form figures (3rd, 2nd) are encouraging and Warren Fentiman's low-key claim adds some value, making him a credible close-up threat.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in four of his last five starts, His Finest Hour arrives here fresh after 17 days, has run over today's trip, and carries 138 lb from stall three; winless in recent starts but his strong profile of seconds and thirds marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in a field that does not suit deep closers, though his recent form includes wins and places over 10f for the same Easterby yard whose current form is excellent; Rhys Elliott's 3lb claim helps and his soft-going run (5th) was not disgraced.|
runners_data.comment: Yermanthere showed his worth with back-to-back seconds and a win earlier in this run of form, giving him solid recent form, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is that sixth last time out suggests he can find one or two too good.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose soft-going and distance figures are uninspiring (one placing in 15 runs on similar ground); tongue-tie applied but with no wins from his last 10 outings and a modest trainer strike rate, he is hard to enthuse about.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back offers a crumb of comfort for No Knee Never, but he arrives winless in his last six starts and a trainer striking at just 5% in the past fortnight is a concern, even if experience over today's trip and going keeps him in the conversation from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: Has won on good ground over 9-10f and ran placed at 9f on similar; prominent style suits the likely race shape but Shay Farmer's 3lb claim is not particularly reassuring, and his consistency figures — five runs without a win recently — limit confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Draupnir has run over today's trip and going and, with our rating putting him second of seven in this field, he arrives with genuine claims as a leading threat; the worry is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and his recent finishing positions make improvement the key ask.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Straightforward in character and capable of winning on good ground (scored at 10f recently), but his natural hold-up style has been repositioned to midfield on the map purely because the field is saturated with closers; racing out of his comfort zone reduces his chance materially.|
runners_data.comment: Cosmos Raj returns on a quick ten-day turnaround and has run over today's trip and going, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures he faces a stiff task, and four consecutive finishes off the frame in his last six starts before that recent win make him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Precious Spartan
runners_data.note: Soft-ground record (two placed runs from 15) is weak for a horse now asked to handle Ripon soft over 10f; similarly shifted toward midfield because genuine backmarkers are overrepresented, meaning Cian Horgan will struggle to produce him with his preferred late run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an unplaced effort latest and finishes of eighth and ninth in the two runs prior, Precious Spartan faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures; a third four starts back and distance-and-going experience at least offer slim crumbs of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Poet's Dawn is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push her, she is set to dictate a controlled, measured gallop on soft ground over 1m2f at Ripon — a flat, fair track that does not punish leaders who manage their energy well. Triple Force, His Finest Hour, and Draupnir are all prominent types who will likely track Poet's Dawn in the early stages, creating a compact leading group but without the pressure of a pace duel. From the home turn the emphasis will be on those who can travel efficiently through the soft ground and sustain their effort over the final three furlongs, giving the edge to horses with proven soft-ground stamina and clean jumping ability off a true pace. This race shape firmly favours prominent or close-tracking runners with soft-ground credentials, as the controlled early tempo will leave enough in the tank for those just behind the leader to mount a challenge, while true hold-up horses are unlikely to generate the late momentum needed on this surface. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear — Cosmos Raj and Precious Spartan are genuine closers pushed into midfield on the map, and Poet's Dawn alongside Triple Force and His Finest Hour are most likely to actually secure their natural forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poet's Dawn controls throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Poet's Dawn is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a sustainable soft-ground gallop, conserving enough for a strong final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old has won four of her last five starts over this exact 10f trip and arrives just 10 days fresh; on soft she has every chance to outstay rivals if the pace is not forced.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent pair overhaul leader
scenarios.trigger: If Triple Force or His Finest Hour track the pace comfortably and find Poet's Dawn's gallop slowing enough to be pegged back in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: His Finest Hour has twice run second over similar trips and his soft-ground form is encouraging; Triple Force's reappearance after 66 days adds risk but his class at this trip is respected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield stalker delivers late
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground gradually stretches the field and one of the better-placed midfield types, particularly Yermanthere, picks off tiring rivals from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Yermanthere has won over 10f on good and placed on soft, and his Easterby yard is in strong recent form (T14: 6/79); a genuinely-run race on soft could see him finish powerfully through beaten horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses suddenly and a compressed finish creates an opportunity for Cosmos Raj or Precious Spartan to deliver from deep.
scenarios.body: This scenario is markedly discounted because both Cosmos Raj and Precious Spartan are redistributed — they are true hold-up types forced into midfield on the map and unlikely to achieve their natural position; their style-fit penalties (0.93/0.92) further reduce their effectiveness here.

watchPoints.text: Poet's Dawn's soft-ground record is very limited (1 placing from 15 similar-going runs) — if the ground is testing rather than merely soft, her ability to see out the trip at a strong tempo is the single biggest risk to the dominant scenario.
Triple Force returns from 66 days off with zero trainer wins from three recent runners — watch the market closely; if he drifts, fitness concerns are likely and the pace dynamic changes materially.

His Finest Hour is the one horse capable of sitting third or fourth and producing a sustained challenge; if he tracks Poet's Dawn smoothly through the first mile, he is the most dangerous prominent threat to the leader.

Cosmos Raj and Precious Spartan are both genuine closers mapped artificially to midfield — if the early pace collapses and a compressed finish develops, they are technically best-placed of the deep types, but their style displacement means this requires specific circumstances to materialise.

Tim Easterby runs two horses (Poet's Dawn, Yermanthere) — watch for stable jockey alignment and market moves, as his 14-day form (6 wins from 79 runners) suggests the yard is live and either runner could represent intended stable confidence.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Walt
runners_data.note: Soft-ground form reads as 1/2 from two similar-going runs, which is his strongest credential, but as a hold-up horse over five furlongs at Ripon he will need the pace to collapse late — 66 days off adds a small fitness query.|

runners_data.name: Classyfied
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is in sound form (6/79 over 14 days) and Classyfied is a hold-up type whose two runs came on Good ground, meaning soft is an untested variable; only eight days since last run suggests she is fit, but her closing style is a structural disadvantage here.|

runners_data.name: American Psycho
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's runner has a second-place finish on Good at Goodwood in his favour, and while he appears in midfield on the race map, his natural game is to race from further back — the crowded hold-up berths mean he will not get his preferred position, which tempers his prospects in a shape that rewards prominent running.|

runners_data.name: Catavega
runners_data.note: A complete unknown on debut for Michael & David Easterby, who are a yard to respect in northern novice sprints; the going is marked UNKNOWN for style because there is no evidence of how she will race or handle soft, making her genuinely unquantifiable.|

runners_data.name: Empress Princess
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly posted a second on Good at Goodwood on her only start and is the most credentialled prominent-style horse behind The Resdev Roman; Daniel Tudhope takes the ride and she looks the natural beneficiary if the leader weakens.|

runners_data.name: Kumharas
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey debut runner with no public form to assess; style and going suitability are entirely unknown, which makes her a speculative quantity, though the Fahey yard's experience with juvenile sprinters means she cannot be dismissed entirely.|

runners_data.name: The Resdev Roman
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who sets the tempo for the whole race, but two seventh-place finishes on Good ground raise questions about her underlying ability; Joanna Mason rides and the soft surface may suit better than her form suggests, though the STYLE_FIT tag flags that she is operating at the sharp end of her comfort zone.|

races.paceDynamic: The Resdev Roman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner soft-ground novice and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be allowed to dictate from the gates at whatever tempo she chooses on Ripon's straight five furlongs. Soft ground on a flat track typically compresses the field and rewards those who travel comfortably in the first half of the race rather than those forced to make sustained ground from the rear. Empress Princess is the most likely horse to press or track closely from a prominent position, giving The Resdev Roman a degree of company without creating a true pace battle. This shape — a single uncontested leader setting a comfortable but genuine clip — favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can latch onto the pace early and sustain their effort through the testing ground; true hold-up horses will struggle to find the necessary late momentum on soft turf over five furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically get to the rear on their own terms — Walt and Classyfied are natural closers who should fill those back positions, while American Psycho, though a genuine hold-up horse, has been redistributed to midfield on the map as space at the back is already occupied by the confirmed hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Resdev Roman Controls
scenarios.trigger: If The Resdev Roman bowls along uncontested and sets a sustainable soft-ground tempo that suits front-to-prominent racing.
scenarios.body: The Resdev Roman dictates every yard of the contest and the prominent-style Empress Princess tracks in her wake, making this a two-horse duel into the final furlong on tiring ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If The Resdev Roman fades in the final furlong having set too strong a pace for the soft ground, leaving the closely-tracking runners to inherit victory.
scenarios.body: Empress Princess, who has already shown a runner-up finish over course-equivalent conditions at Goodwood, is ideally placed to capitalise as the leader ties up; the unknown quantities Catavega and Kumharas, both lightly raced, could emerge if they show natural prominent inclinations from the gate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses badly late and the genuinely soft-ground-effective closers get a clear run through the field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Walt and Classyfied are the authentic hold-up horses in this field and both have soft-ground form to call on, giving them the best claims if a late surge is rewarded; however, five furlongs on soft at Ripon rarely produces enough late compression for true closers to pick up from off the pace, making this scenario genuinely unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or both of Catavega or Kumharas, racing for the first time, show unexpectedly sharp gate-to-wire ability and outclass the experienced runners.
scenarios.body: Unraced runners occasionally burst clear on debut when handled by shrewd trainers — Michael & David Easterby saddle Catavega and Richard & Peter Fahey send out Kumharas — but the complete absence of form data makes this a low-confidence outcome that is hard to price meaningfully.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether The Resdev Roman gets a clean break from the stalls — if she misses the kick, there is no other confirmed leader to set the race up and the entire pace shape collapses.

Empress Princess is on just her second career start with 19 days between runs; if Daniel Tudhope gets her settled immediately behind the leader, she is ideally placed, but inexperience over soft ground could see her hang or idle.
Both debutants Catavega and Kumharas are completely unknown quantities — if either shows natural early speed, they could disrupt The Resdev Roman's uncontested lead sooner than anticipated.

Walt and Classyfied are the two genuine hold-up horses and both will need to be delivered very late; on soft ground over five furlongs at Ripon, monitor in the final 100 yards whether the pace genuinely collapses enough to give them a winning run.

American Psycho's redistribution to midfield means his jockey Pierre-Louis Jamin may find he cannot slot into his preferred position early — watch for crowding or shuffling back in the first furlong as the hold-up contingent sorts itself out.

races.name: 21 Engineer Regiment Sapper Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lexington Boom
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner with form figures of 1-2-2 on good ground at 5f, giving it the best recent profile of the lead horses; Grant Tuer's yard is out of form (0/12 in 14 days) which is a genuine concern, but the horse's natural gate speed makes it the most credible early leader.|
runners_data.comment: Lexington Boom arrives in fine nick, winning last time out and filling the runner-up spot in two of his three subsequent starts, with experience over today's trip and a lively weight-to-rating profile adding further appeal.

runners_data.name: Roman Crystal
runners_data.note: Drops back to 5f having run all its recent races over 6f on good ground, and a glance at those figures (6-5-4-3-1 in reverse) shows improvement coming but the drop in trip on soft ground is an untested combination; Billy Garritty rides and this horse is likely to be crowded out in the battle for the early lead.|
runners_data.comment: Roman Crystal arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, with 24 days between runs suggesting she comes here fresh and ready; the main risk is that her speed rating of 65 leaves her with something to find against the top-rated runner.

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: Arrived at her last two wins over 6f on good ground, but her sole soft-ground entry (2/7 in similar-going history, 0 wins 0 places) is a flag worth watching; Ollie Pears' yard is firing at 2/8 in 14 days, Harry Russell takes the ride, and the headgear notation (p) suggests a sheepskin/cheekpiece that may help her travel prominently.|
runners_data.comment: Lady Dublin won back-to-back races three and two starts back, and with experience over today's trip and our rating putting her top of these rivals, she looks the one to beat; the worry is that disappointing eighth last time out.

runners_data.name: Star People
runners_data.note: Blinkers applied (hg:b) and this is a horse that has contested every pace so far in its career, finishing 2-3-2-5-10 in reverse — a front-runner by nature who comes back to 5f after 6f runs; John & Sean Quinn are placing runners well (4/17 in 14 days) and Star People is quick enough to contest the lead from the jump, but must sustain it on soft.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in fine nick, Star People brings strong claims here: second last time out and again three starts back, with experience over today's trip and a quick 12-day turnaround suggesting he's in good order. The main risk is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: May Bee In Profit
runners_data.note: The one runner in the field with a genuine soft-ground placing on record (2nd/5f/Soft), making this the standout profile advantage in the race; David Allan rides for Tim Easterby whose stable is in strong form (6/79 in 14 days), and a prominent style means May Bee In Profit can sit just off the contested lead and let the chaos unfold ahead.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, May Bee In Profit has shown some ability — a winner and placed efforts feature in recent starts — but a sixth and an unplaced run since make her hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's trip and returns fit enough at 12 days.

runners_data.name: Inca Warrior
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's juvenile has only run twice (both fourths on good ground at 5f) and returns after 45 days; a natural prominent racer, Inca Warrior is shown further back in the mapping simply because every other slot ahead of it is filled with more pace-committed rivals, and Rowan Scott will need to decide early whether to push forward or settle — the style fit discount (0.87) reflects that neither option is truly natural.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Inca Warrior faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip before and a 45-day break may have freshened him from stall one at 128 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Star People, Lexington Boom, and Roman Crystal are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing an aggressive, contested pace from the outset over this 5f on soft ground at Ripon — a combination that will place maximum stamina demands on every runner in this small field. The lead will be fought for vigorously from the gates, and soft ground will amplify the energy cost of that early battle, meaning those who do secure the front will be doing so at a price. Lady Dublin and May Bee In Profit sit just off the pace as prominent types, giving them a marginal energy advantage if the front trio burn each other out inside the final two furlongs. The race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners with soft-ground credentials who can produce a sustained, grinding finish rather than a sharp turn of foot, as the contested early pace will almost certainly compromise the leadersᅥ reserves — the field holds more front-running types than can all get their preferred position, and Lexington Boom (most recent strong form) and Star People (highest RPR-equivalent, blinkers) are best placed to actually secure the early lead, with Roman Crystal the most likely to be shuffled back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fight for position and drain each other's stamina through the first half of the race on soft ground, allowing a prominent tracker to mow them down.
scenarios.body: The burning early pace saps the leaders' reserves in the testing conditions, and a horse racing just off the front can pick up the pieces in the final furlong as the leaders tie up. Soft ground punishes any horse that has over-exerted in the first half, making this the dominant shape given three confirmed lead horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Dominant Front-Runner Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners (most likely Lexington Boom or Star People) surges clear early and establishes a rhythm that the others cannot sustain, controlling the race from the front.
scenarios.body: Whichever front-runner settles into a controlled lead after the initial scramble can exploit the soft ground at their own pace rather than a frantic one, preserving enough energy to hold on through the final furlong. Lexington Boom's recent winning form and Star People's blinkered determination make them the likeliest candidates to convert from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce but not completely suicidal, and a prominent racer at the head of the chasing group produces a relentless, grinding finish to collar a weakening leader close home.
scenarios.body: Lady Dublin's back-to-back winning form on good ground and May Bee In Profit's soft-ground placing give both a profile that suits a sustained gallop rather than a sprint finish. On soft ground over 5f with a strong pace, those tracking the pace two lengths off the lead through the middle stages are set up perfectly for a grinding late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely implodes and Inca Warrior, operating out of its natural prominent role and mapped further back, gets a dream run through a faltering field.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Inca Warrior racing in a genuinely held-up role, which is not its natural style, making it structurally unlikely to execute the move required. The horse's limited form (two fourth-place finishes on good ground, 45 days off) provides little confidence it has the class to overhaul rivals even if the ideal scenario materialises.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a fractious, ragged start — with Star People, Lexington Boom, and Roman Crystal all wanting the early lead, there is a real risk of bumping and crowding in the first furlong that could compromise any or all three front-runners before the race has properly begun.

Roman Crystal's switch from 6f good ground to 5f soft is the most significant surface-and-trip combination shift in the field — if it fails to find its stride quickly, Billy Garritty may be caught in a no-man's land between the pace and the chasers.

Lady Dublin's similar-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 7 runs) despite her back-to-back wins on good ground means the soft Ripon surface could blunt her finishing effort — watch whether she travels as fluently as she has on better ground.

May Bee In Profit's 45-day absence (Inca Warrior) and 12-day turnaround are at opposite ends of the freshness spectrum — monitor market moves on Inca Warrior in the hour before the race as any stable confidence would be reflected in a shortening price despite the layoff.

The three-way battle for the lead means sectional times in the first two furlongs will be exceptionally fast relative to soft-ground norms — any horse that gets taken off its feet in the early scramble and cannot settle into a rhythm is at serious risk of stopping abruptly in the final furlong.

races.name: Ripon Yorkshire's Garden Racecourse Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Reigning Profit
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for Ruth Carr who won on good ground over 5f at Goodwood recently but has a thin record in soft conditions (0 wins, 0 places from 3 soft/heavy runs); the step up to 6f is a minor query given all her best form is at 5f.
runners_data.comment: Reigning Profit has finished eighth last time out and was unplaced two starts back, and with our rating placing him eighth of ten runners he is hard to fancy at the weights; experience over today's trip and going is a slim but genuine foothold.

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who showed a placed effort at 6f on good ground and has soft-going form showing a win and two places from four attempts; Tom Eaves takes over and the yard has had a quiet 14-day spell, but the profile suits this race shape well.
runners_data.comment: Arduis Invicta showed plenty when finishing second three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going is a genuine asset at 136 lb from stall nine; the concern is she has been winless in recent starts, with a couple of unplaced efforts among her recent runs to account for.

runners_data.name: Charlie Mason
runners_data.note: Has a win in soft-ground conditions and Tony Carroll's operation has been busy and in form over 14 days; however, this horse is a genuine hold-up type racing in a field where securing that position will be difficult, meaning the natural style is likely to be compromised from the outset.
runners_data.comment: Charlie Mason won four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, so conditions pose no obvious concern; at 134 lb from stall 4, the weight burden is the key question after three unplaced efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's higher-rated hold-up horse (OR 81) who has finished in the places consistently at this trip on good ground; only 4 days since his last run is a slight fitness query, and with just 2 runs in similar going he is relatively unexposed on soft, but his position in the race will be dictated by the lack of pace in front of him.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and twice more in recent starts, Yes I'm Mali arrives just four days on from that effort carrying 141 lb from stall 10, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; yet to win in his last six starts, but his rating of 88 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Top Juggler
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 6f on good and placed on soft; Seb Spencer's horse sets the entire tempo of this race and on soft going at a flat track the style-fit flag (0.93) reflects that his lead role becomes his greatest asset rather than a concern — the horse is genuinely in control of its own destiny.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and was second three starts back, but a seventh last time out clouds the picture; has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days between runs suggests he returns fresh enough, though 139 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Kind Touch
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained three-year-old with a win and a place in soft-going conditions from only five prior runs, giving a small but meaningful soft-ground sample; 52 days off the track is worth monitoring, but the hold-up style with Oisin Orr aboard could see this horse delivered with a well-timed late run if the pace proves honest enough.

runners_data.name: Anaisa
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby juvenile whose recent form string shows mainly mid-field finishes on good ground; wears a hood (hg:t) and has the fewest credentials in similar going of the hold-up horses, making it difficult to construct a winning scenario for this runner in the current race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Anaisa has nonetheless shown consistent midfield form with a pair of fourths and a fifth in that spell, and she has experience over today's distance and going; at 133 lb from stall seven, there is plenty to do, but a 17-day turnaround keeps her fresh.

runners_data.name: Secret Guest
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's six-year-old has managed only one in-the-money finish in the last five starts and the form string (865004) is not encouraging; a genuine hold-up runner whose natural position is at the rear of the field, and in a race where that territory is crowded and the pace is not extreme, the route to a winning run is very narrow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Secret Guest nevertheless rates a shade above his official mark on our figures and has run over today's trip and going before; the fourth last time out offers a crumb of encouragement, though his overall recent record makes it hard to fancy him strongly from stall three carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's seven-year-old holds multiple second-place finishes at this course and trip, hinting at a consistent if frustrating profile; the hold-up style is authentic and the horse's own runners are placed to the midfield on the map because the rear is full — that displacement makes it harder for this horse to produce the finish its placed record suggests it is capable of.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts despite a run of three consecutive runner-up finishes a couple of starts back, Another Investment has since slipped to sixth and ranks ninth of ten on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Easterby's six-year-old wears a hood (hg:b) and has strong placed form on good ground at both 5f and 6f but barely any comparable soft-ground record (1 run); pushed forward on the map from its natural closing position, the horse will struggle to replicate its best form if it cannot settle into the rear and produce a clean finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Spirit Of Applause faces a stiff task as the bottom-ranked runner on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh ten-day break carrying 129 lb from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Top Juggler is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, honest gallop on soft ground over six furlongs at Ripon — a track where a steady pace from the front is a legitimate winning position. Reigning Profit and Arduis Invicta are the most likely to press Top Juggler for prominent positions, giving the leader a degree of company without generating a true speed duel that would undermine their own chance. The majority of the field are natural hold-up horses — Charlie Mason, Secret Guest, Another Investment and Spirit Of Applause are all genuine closers redistributed into the midfield map because there are simply too many hold-up types for the race shape to accommodate them all in their natural position, and on soft ground at a flat track that does not naturally draw out a strong late kick, their prospects are compromised. This race shape — a single, uncontested pace-setter controlling fractions on soft going — strongly favours horses who can track the leader prominently and sustain their effort, rather than those required to produce a finish from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Top Juggler Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Top Juggler is allowed to stride clear from the gates and sets a soft, honest gallop that plays to his own strengths on this ground.
scenarios.body: Top Juggler leads at his own pace, the soft going blunts any late challenge, and the horse who can stay closest throughout into the straight lands the prize; prominent types who travel into the race with minimal fuss are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and the front pair tire in the final furlong, allowing close-tracking horses to run over them.
scenarios.body: Arduis Invicta or Kind Touch, travelling prominently and conserving energy through the race, find enough to collar a tiring leader inside the final furlong; the soft ground rewards those who switch off early and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses in the final quarter-mile and the closers get an unusual amount of soft-ground momentum.
scenarios.body: Yes I'm Mali, the strongest-rated hold-up horse in the field, represents the best hope among the genuine closers if a gap materialises late; this scenario is materially discounted because the true hold-up runners — Charlie Mason, Secret Guest, Another Investment and Spirit Of Applause — are racing out of natural position and are unlikely to find clear runs in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Fold
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground is more testing than times suggest and both the leader and prominent horses tie up, producing a rough-and-tumble finish.
scenarios.body: An unlikely but possible scenario in deteriorating soft conditions where attrition through the race reshuffles the order in the final stages; lower-weighted, hold-up types coming with late momentum could grab places though a clean winner from this group is hard to identify.

watchPoints.text: Top Juggler's sole lead is the single most important factor in this race — if he breaks cleanly and is allowed to dictate fractions unchallenged, he controls the outcome for the majority of the field.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Charlie Mason, Secret Guest, Another Investment and Spirit Of Applause — will all be competing for the same late ground; watch for traffic problems in the straight that could stop any one of them producing a run even if conditions suit.

Yes I'm Mali ran just 4 days ago and, while David O'Meara manages busy horses well, watch the market for any sign that the quick turnaround has left a mark — if he runs below OR 81 form it removes the most credible hold-up challenger.

Kind Touch is 52 days off the track for the Fahey yard, which has been active over the past fortnight; a market move or strong morning-line support would suggest the stable is confident the horse is ready to show its soft-ground form on return.

Soft going is confirmed across all races at Ripon today — monitor whether the ground description moves to heavy by this race slot, which would further compress the pace and increase the premium on a front-running or close-tracking style.

races.name: Ripon Yorkshire's Garden Racecourse Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Here Forever
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner who will attempt to lead from the off; three-year-old who has won on good ground at this trip but has no soft-ground win in the book — that stamina query under these conditions is the primary concern if the early gallop is hot.|
runners_data.comment: Here Forever has managed one win in his last five starts and, ranked ninth of ten on our figures, is hard to fancy at these weights, though he has run over today's trip before and the run fifty-seven days ago leaves room for improvement.

runners_data.name: Farandaway
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer at six and seven furlongs, twice a winner over this trip, and brings recent soft-ground placing (2/6f/Soft) that gives him a meaningful edge in the conditions; T14 record of 0/12 for Grant Tuer is a concern for those wanting trainer confidence, but the horse's own form does the talking.|
runners_data.comment: Farandaway has winning form in recent starts and returns on a quick turnaround just ten days after his last run, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour, but ranked eighth of ten on our figures he faces a stiff ask at 134 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Wobwobwob
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with genuine soft-ground form (three places from 15 runs in similar conditions), though the pattern of fading in the finish is a consistent flag and the form string of -09509 suggests he needs things to fall perfectly; fitted with tongue-tie.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with a pair of ninths and two unplaced efforts among them, Wobwobwob makes little appeal from stall six carrying 133 lb, and our rating of 72 ranks him last of ten; experience over today's trip and going, plus a sharp 11-day turnaround, offer scant consolation.

runners_data.name: Almarada Prince
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has twice finished second or placed at this trip on good ground, including a second at 6f on good, but the sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 15 runs in soft-comparable conditions is a stark caution; David Nolan's booking adds jockey quality.|
runners_data.comment: Almarada Prince shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out, and third three starts back underlines his consistency at this level; rated 84 by us, he carries 140 lb from stall one, and the chief concern is that he remains yet to win in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Venture Capital
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with a hood, and despite poor recent form (-87089) Kevin Ryan's yard is in form (3/34 over 14 days); most of his recent runs have come over five furlongs on better ground, making this step back to six on soft a notable question.|
runners_data.comment: Venture Capital returns after 31 days with experience over today's trip and going in his favour, and our rating of 87 marks him as the one to beat in a field of ten, though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to find improvement to justify that standing.

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pacesetter types, and crucially the one with an actual win on soft ground (1W from 9 runs in similar conditions); Daniel Tudhope is a significant jockey advantage and the tongue-tie adds a headgear angle; his challenge depends on whether he can escape the duel with Here Forever.|
runners_data.comment: Goyard arrives on the back of a fifth last time out and has been winless in his last five starts, though a third four starts back offers a flicker of encouragement; he has distance and going experience and returns after a 21-day break carrying 137 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a recent second at 6f on good, making him the most course-suited of the pace-tracking group; the Tim Easterby yard is in very strong form (6/79 over 14 days) and the blinkered headgear should ensure he races prominently — a horse to keep onside in Scenario A.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mister Sox does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and steps back up having shaped with a little more promise when second and third in earlier efforts, though back-to-back fifths most recently are hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Fortamour
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up specialist whose best result in the past five is a second at 6f on good, but three of his last five have been double-figure finishes; no wins or places from 15 runs on comparable soft ground makes him hard to recommend in any scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Fortamour shaped with promise when second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead from stall seven carrying 132 lb; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: First Folio
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true style sees him closer to the rear than the map suggests; visor applied, and Julie Camacho's runner has some placing at 6f on good, but the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects that he is unlikely to get his preferred position in this pace-contested race, reducing his chance accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, First Folio nevertheless catches the eye with a rating of 82 that puts him well clear of his official mark, and he has run over today's distance and going before; the worry is that his recent record offers little encouragement of a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Educating Rita
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has shown she can place (twice third in recent form) but her hold-up profile means she too is racing out of role given how many back-of-field types are in this field; Philip Kirby's yard is lightly in-form and there are no soft-ground wins in her record to suggest the conditions will compensate for the tactical compromise.|
runners_data.comment: Educating Rita has shown she can hit the frame, with thirds two and five starts back, but has otherwise struggled for consistency and remains yet to win in her last five starts; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 17 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Here Forever and Goyard are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both drawn in a field of ten on soft ground over six furlongs at Ripon, an early tussle for the lead is near-certain — neither is a horse that will volunteer to settle off the pace. That contested early fractions will set an honest, potentially draining gallop on softening ground, which historically at Ripon's flat, straight six favours horses who can travel prominently without burning fuel in the battle, rather than those forced to chase hard from behind. Farandaway, Venture Capital, and Mister Sox represent the prominent brigade who can slot in just off the two leaders and exploit the honest pace without being embroiled in the duel itself. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate, with First Folio and Educating Rita pushed into midfield on the map despite being natural closers — given the pace duel up front, late closers will have a genuine target, but soft-ground efficiency and prominent positioning are the keys; this race shape most favours horses racing just off the pace who can pick up when the front-running pair inevitably tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Pair Tire, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Here Forever and Goyard fight for the lead and burn each other out on soft ground, leaving the prominent stalkers to pick up the pieces in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop on soft turf saps both leaders turning for home, and a horse like Farandaway — who has shown a knack for winning off an honest pace — tracks into a winning position without having to find a finishing kick from deep. Mister Sox and Venture Capital also profile as beneficiaries of this shape, sitting close enough to lead but not engaged in the duel itself.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Dictates, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners (most likely Goyard, who has a win on soft) gets a clear lead and the other capitulates early, leaving a single horse to control a sustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: With a lone pacer setting a measured fractions on soft, the race becomes more about class and stamina than raw speed, and the controlling horse can conserve enough energy to hold on. Goyard has soft-ground form to call upon and a top jockey in Tudhope who will exploit any drift in the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is truly brutal and the leaders collapse dramatically inside the final furlong, giving genuine ground to horses held up or sitting midfield.
scenarios.body: Almarada Prince, who has shown course-and-distance placing, could emerge as the best of the hold-up types if the pace collapse is severe enough; Wobwobwob has soft-ground form and could pick up late. However, First Folio and Educating Rita — true hold-up types displaced into midfield — face the additional burden of racing out of their natural role, which reduces the reliability of this shape delivering via those horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the entire field races at a punishing pace and a late swooper finds an unobstructed path through a tiring field in the final strides.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends heavily on hold-up types racing from their true position, but First Folio and Educating Rita are displaced from the rear and face a compromised shape; even if they get closest late, they are doing so out of role and with less advantage than a genuine scenario of this kind would offer. The probability is low precisely because the horses best-placed to win this shape are not running from their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Here Forever and Goyard are on a collision course for the lead — watch whether one backs off within the first furlong or whether both commit fully, as the latter outcome is the single biggest swing factor in how far the prominent stalkers benefit.
Farandaway's trainer Grant Tuer has gone 0 from 12 runners in the past 14 days — if there is any market drift on this horse at the off, that stable form stat may be the reason why.

Venture Capital has run predominantly over five furlongs recently and steps back to six on soft ground — watch his price in the market as an indicator of whether connections are confident this step up in trip on this surface is intentional and prepared for.

Mister Sox's trainer Tim Easterby has had 6 winners from 79 runners in the past 14 days — one of the stronger stable form reads in this race and worth noting if the horse is prominent early and still travelling at the two-furlong pole.

Wobwobwob is tagged as fading in the finish — if the soft ground slows the overall pace and he is closer than usual at the halfway point, watch whether he sustains it or drops away inside the final furlong as his profile suggests he typically does.

races.name: attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Blinkers-equipped veteran front runner for Tim Easterby who has been racing exclusively at Goodwood on good ground; similar-going record is poor (0 wins, 0 places from 15), and at age 11 the soft ground represents a significant concern — the chief value here is the pace she sets rather than the result she achieves.
runners_data.comment: Garden Oasis has been consistently knocking at the door, finishing third, third, and second in his last three starts, and our rating of 80 puts him among the very best in this field; the risk is that he remains winless and may again find one too good.

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride for David O'Meara on this prominent racer whose recent form at Goodwood on good ground reads consistently mid-division; the step back to soft is neutral on stats, but tracking a contested pace from the front rank is exactly the tactical position she needs and Tudhope will be alive to that opportunity.
runners_data.comment: Donna Nook shaped with promise when third last time out and is a winner in her last six starts, with experience over today's trip and a fitness edge at just 18 days since her latest run; her rating of 81 marks her as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Catton Lady
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this hold-up mare who is the standout soft-ground performer in the field with 2 wins and 4 places from 15 similar-going runs; most recently won over 7f soft and placed at 8f soft, so the trip and conditions are right, and the contested pace suits a closer — though she will need to weave through 12 rivals from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Catton Lady arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims here, and she carries 139 lb from stall nine as the main threat to her chances.

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's hold-up filly has only one run on similar going (a placing at Catterick) but won last time at Goodwood over this trip; Kevin Stott rides and she has placed on soft before, though her form overall suggests good ground is preferred and the field is competitive enough to make her task hard from the back.
runners_data.comment: Kiss Me My Love has placed third last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, but an unplaced effort three starts back tempers confidence; carrying 137 lb from stall 3, she holds claims without being certain to improve on a mixed recent profile.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's 5-year-old has 1 win and 3 places from 15 similar-going runs and steps back down from 10f to 1m, which looks a positive given his second at 8f good; Oliver Stammers rides for a yard with 0/12 in the 14-day window — steady trainer form, but the soft ground profile is encouraging and tracking from prominent is his style.
runners_data.comment: Bellasio showed ability when winning two starts back, but his latest run was unplaced and, ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, he faces a stiff task at 134 lb, though he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Thornaby Annie
runners_data.note: 3-year-old for Adrian Nicholls wearing hood, whose entire form has come on good ground with just a single placing on similar going from 12 runs; Jack Nicholls takes the 3lb claim and she has placed three times over this trip, but the soft ground question is real and she may not get the position she needs from a crowded field.
runners_data.comment: Thornaby Annie showed plenty when a second two starts back, but a seventh last time out clouds her chance here; she has run over today's trip and a 34-day break leaves fitness mildly in question, though she carries 133 lb from stall 13 with a rating edge over her mark.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Joy
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's 4-year-old is a genuine hold-up type but has been mapped into midfield because the field is overloaded with horses wanting the same rear positions; returning from 57 days off with a single similar-going run in the book (unplaced), her chance is conditional on getting a clean run she is unlikely to find in a big field off a soft-ground honest pace — the style-fit discount is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Hopeful Joy has been out of the frame in three of her four most recent outings, and 57 days off the track adds a fitness query; experience over today's trip is about the best that can be said for her.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's 3-year-old has placed four times in eight soft-ground runs including twice at 7f soft this season, showing clear affinity for testing conditions; a natural hold-up horse in a field where the rear is congested, the stable's four runners today creates potential for some deliberate positional awareness, and the distance step up from 7f to 1m is untested.
runners_data.comment: Milford Grange has experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 74 puts him ahead of his official mark — a solid case that he retains untapped ability, though he has been winless in his last six starts and must bounce back from a fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Paroda Diva
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to race prominently — her headgear note (p) and recent win at 8f soft underline genuine soft-ground ability and form — but with Garden Oasis, Penny Ghent and Donna Nook already filling the front ranks, Andrew Mullen will struggle to get her into a rhythm anywhere near her preferred berth; the soft-ground win is tempting but positional compromise is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Paroda Diva won three starts back but was sixth last time out, leaving her form difficult to assess heading here; she has run over today's trip and returns after 22 days, though her speed rating of 64 may leave her with ground to make up from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's 3-year-old prefers to race prominently but the map has pushed him into midfield given the traffic ahead; his recent form reads 5-0040 with no wins or places on similar going, and David Nolan cannot manufacture a position that the race shape will not give him — minimal claims here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Zermatt Star does at least return after a 26-day break with experience over today's trip in her favour, though a fourth two starts back represents her best recent effort and she faces a stiff task from draw seven carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: G'Emmethegreenlite
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's 3-year-old, freshest in the field at 13 days since last run, wears a tongue tie and has been running over shorter trips (5-6f) all season before stepping up to 1m for the first time; the unexplored stamina question on soft ground, combined with being squeezed out of a natural front-forward position by genuine pacemakers, makes this very hard to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures, G'Emmethegreenlite faces a stiff ask here; a ninth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround of 13 days.

runners_data.name: Gunalt Wavelength
runners_data.note: A lightly raced 3-year-old who has won twice and placed six times from 14 similar-going runs, showing the best soft-ground record among the horses mapped to midfield; Shay Farmer's 5lb claim is useful, but his natural home is closer to the pace than the map allows and the style compromise tempers what his going form suggests — worth monitoring how he is ridden from stall.
runners_data.comment: Gunalt Wavelength won two of her last five starts, with a fourth and sixth in more recent outings suggesting she may need things to fall right, though she has experience over today's trip and going, and 38 days between runs keeps fitness under scrutiny.

runners_data.name: Penny Ghent
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's 6-year-old is a confirmed front runner with blinkers and two recent wins at this trip and course combination; her similar-going record is poor (0/15) which is a genuine worry given today's soft conditions, and Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim saves weight but she may find the sustained battle for the lead with Garden Oasis too costly to sustain deep into the race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Penny Ghent faces a stiff ask here, though she does arrive with two wins in her last six starts and has run over today's trip and going before, offering some small crumbs of comfort from stall two off 34 days.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Oasis and Penny Ghent are the two confirmed front runners, and with both holding blinkers and genuine early-pace profiles, a contested lead is almost certain from the off on this soft Ripon mile. The likely outcome is an honest, unrelenting gallop that stretches the field from the back of Ripon's long sweeping bend, leaving hold-up horses needing significant late momentum to close — momentum that soft ground will cost them. Prominent racers who can track the pace just off the leaders without burning out in the battle for the lead hold the strongest tactical position here. Several runners tagged as redistributed — Zermatt Star, Paroda Diva, G'Emmethegreenlite, and Gunalt Wavelength — are genuine prominent or hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural position given the traffic in front of them, meaning the field holds more pace than the map can cleanly accommodate; Garden Oasis and Penny Ghent are most likely to actually lead, with Donna Nook best placed to lock onto the speed from just behind. This race shape unequivocally favours prominent-to-midfield horses with strong soft-ground form who can survive the gallop and pick up in the straight, with pure closers disadvantaged by the combination of contested pace and testing ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis and Penny Ghent fight for the lead and set a genuine honest gallop that strings the field out on soft ground.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other up through the first half-mile, creating a true-run race where a prominent racer just off the speed can exploit their tiring effort in the final two furlongs; soft ground rewards those who have settled just behind rather than fought for the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Best
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is severe enough to exhaust the leaders and any prominent horses, opening the race up for a true late finisher.
scenarios.body: Soft ground slows the overall tempo sufficiently in the back straight that a genuine hold-up horse can still generate the closing kick needed; however, most true closers in this field are redistributed and racing out of role, which limits how likely this outcome is.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Penny Ghent or Garden Oasis breaks cleaner or the other capitulates early, leaving one to dictate at a controlled pace on the soft going.
scenarios.body: An unchallenged leader on soft ground can find a comfortable rhythm that saps the finishing kick of hold-up horses and leaves prominent chasers just short; this is less likely given how evenly matched both front runners appear on ratings and intent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race or the field fans wide, allowing a midfield runner with soft-ground credentials to pick through.
scenarios.body: Soft going can occasionally compress the pace enough in the middle portions of a race to let midfield types accelerate past a strung-out and tiring lead group; Milford Grange and Gunalt Wavelength have shown placing form in soft conditions that could make them threats if the shape unfolds this way, though both are racing at least partially out of their natural role here.

watchPoints.text: Both Garden Oasis and Penny Ghent are confirmed front runners with blinkers — watch the early stalls break closely because whichever gains the rail and first stride will control the tempo; if neither yields, the pace could be fierce enough to compromise every prominent racer.

Catton Lady is the standout on soft-ground form (2W 4P from 15 similar-going runs) but is a genuine hold-up horse in a 13-runner field — watch whether Joanna Mason can find a clear passage around the bend, as any crowding will cost her the momentum she needs on this ground.

Gunalt Wavelength has the best soft-ground placing record among the redistributed horses (6 runs, 2 places) and Shay Farmer takes the 5lb claim — watch where he is positioned at the start, because if he can get closer to the pace than his map position suggests, his conditions form makes him a live each-way threat.

Donna Nook's trainer David O'Meara has 3 winners from 40 runners in the 14-day window and Daniel Tudhope is a high-quality booking — watch whether she travels smoothly in the prominent group, because if the leaders tie each other up, she is ideally poised to capitalise in the straight.

The Michael & David Easterby yard saddles three runners (Catton Lady, Milford Grange, Gunalt Wavelength) — watch for any signs of stable confidence or market moves among the trio, as a shrewd yard running multiple horses in the same race can sometimes engineer a positional advantage for one at the expense of the others.

races.name: Wakeman Stayers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with decent placed form over 14-17f on good ground, but soft-going record is poor (0 wins, 0 places from 3 runs on similar), which is a significant concern today; Micky Hammond has a fair 14-day strike rate and Aiden Brookes takes over, but this horse likely needs a faster surface to show its best.
runners_data.comment: Twilight Safari arrives here on the back of a runner-up finish last time out, and a third three starts back underlines his consistency in recent outings; yet to win in his last five starts, he rates our top pick on a mark of 77 and has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Zimmerman
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer with consistent form at 16-17f on good ground and a tidy soft-going record of 4 from 15; 85 days off the track is the main risk, though Tim Easterby's yard (T14: 6/79) is firing and David Allan knows this horse well.
runners_data.comment: Zimmerman has shown consistent improvement in recent starts, placing second and third earlier in the campaign before a sixth last time out, and has experience over today's distance and going; the main concern is 85 days off the track, though he looks a strong threat at the weights carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Bollin Neil
runners_data.note: The only true front-runner in the field and 223 days off the track is a notable concern, but he has soft-ground experience over staying trips and with no pace rival to push him, a ten-year-old who knows how to lead is perfectly positioned to exploit this race shape; Jake Dickson claims 5lb.
runners_data.comment: Bollin Neil brings back-to-back wins into this, scoring two starts and three starts back respectively, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is a 223-day absence which leaves his current fitness very much the question.

runners_data.name: Dereham
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature pushed into a midfield slot on the map by field congestion, operating well below his natural comfort zone positionally; John Berry's yard is cold at T14 (0/2) and soft-going placed form is scant (1 from 15), so the tactical compromise adds to already limited credentials.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and again five starts back, Dereham returns in good order after 24 days and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Femme Fatale
runners_data.note: The yard (James Tate, T14: 4/18) and Daniel Tudhope in the saddle give confidence, and she arrives on the back of a 16f Southwell win; naturally prominent in style and well-suited to tracking a lone front-runner, though her soft-ground form (0 wins, 0 places from 3 runs) is worth monitoring on today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Won last time over 16f at Southwell in headgear and arrives only 15 days later, which is positive freshness; a true hold-up horse squeezed into midfield by this crowded rear, meaning she is less likely to get the late-charging scenario she needs, and her good-ground bias further tempers enthusiasm on soft today.
runners_data.comment: Regally Blonde is ranked bottom of six on our figures and her recent form is patchy, with just one win in her last six starts, though that victory came last time out and she returns on a fresh 15-day break with distance and going experience in her favour.

runners_data.name: Si White
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Sir Mark Prescott (T14: 6/15, the best return in this field) with a progressive profile including a win at 11f at Southwell, though all his form has come on standard Polytrack — this is his first turf run and first time on soft ground, which represents a significant unknown over 2m.
runners_data.comment: Si White scrambles home a winner three starts back but has finished fifth and third since, and our rating of 62 ranks him fifth of six here, making him hard to fancy at these weights; he has run over today's trip and returns after 24 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Bollin Neil is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, he will stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over this 2m trip on soft ground at Ripon. At a sustainable gallop dictated entirely on his own terms, he sets a rhythm that is unlikely to be breakneck — soft ground over two miles on a flat track rewards economical front-running rather than punishing it. Femme Fatale is the only prominent-style runner likely to sit close to him in second or third, leaving the remainder — Twilight Safari, Zimmerman, and the redistributed hold-up types — to organise themselves in the chasing pack. This shape strongly favours the front-runner and horses with proven prominent or pressing profiles, as the pace will be controlled and moderate enough that late closers will need to work hard through softened ground to peg back a horse with a clear positional advantage. Note that Si White, Dereham, and Regally Blonde are genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield on the map because the rear positions are genuinely crowded — none of them is likely to secure the truly deep hold-up berth their natural style requires, which further undermines the prospect of a late-closing result.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bollin Neil Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bollin Neil bowls into an uncontested lead and controls pace on his own terms throughout the 2m trip.
scenarios.body: He dictates a measured, soft-ground gallop from the front, conserving enough energy to hold on as his rivals struggle through testing ground to close him down in the straight; at OR 59 and with proven soft-ground form, he is well-placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Presser Overhauls Late
scenarios.trigger: If Femme Fatale or Twilight Safari tracks Bollin Neil closely enough to produce a sustained late challenge through the straight.
scenarios.body: A rider who has kept close contact without burning fuel tracks the leader around the final turn and grinds past in the stamina-sapping straight; Femme Fatale's recent winning form over 16f at Southwell and Twilight Safari's consistent placed efforts at similar trips make both credible pressers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Scrambles Order
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched hold-up brigade — Si White, Dereham, Regally Blonde — disrupt each other's positioning and one secures a cleaner run than expected.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural deepest roles, these horses burn more energy than ideal jostling for midfield positions, but Si White's yard (Sir Mark Prescott, T14: 6/15) and improving juvenile profile offers the best upside if he settles well and finds clear daylight entering the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapses Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop on soft ground proves more taxing than expected and Bollin Neil's stamina reserve gives out in the final furlong, gifting a fresh-legged closer.
scenarios.body: Soft ground over two miles can expose a ten-year-old front-runner's limitations when the race has taken enough out of him by the home turn; a hold-up runner with genuine resolution through testing conditions — notably Zimmerman, proven over 16-17f on good — could pick up the pieces if he switches off early enough.

watchPoints.text: Bollin Neil has been off the track for 223 days — watch the market closely to see if connections are confident he returns fit enough to utilise his positional advantage.

Si White's entire form base is on Southwell Polytrack and this is his first start on turf in soft conditions over 2m — if he fails to adapt to the surface, his odds may misrepresent his actual chance.
Femme Fatale holds a prominent-style profile that suits tracking Bollin Neil, but her 0-from-3 record on soft ground is a genuine red flag given today's conditions at Ripon.

Zimmerman has been off 85 days yet Tim Easterby's stable is running at 6/79 over the last 14 days — check if Zimmerman has had a pipe-opener or shows market confidence before accepting his hold-up claims at face value.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Si White, Dereham, Regally Blonde) are likely to jostle for midfield real estate rather than settle in the deep rear — watch early positioning to see whether any actually achieves the clean, settled trip their running style demands.
